national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 205 India marks 10th anniversary of surgical strikes on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan
national_raw_news.content: India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes that demonstrated to the world a new example of the Narendra Modi government’s counter-terrorism policy. On September 28-29, 2016, the Indian Army carried out targeted surgical strikes on terrorist launch pads across the Line of Control (LoC) in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The operation was launched as a direct and decisive military response to the Uri terror attack earlier that month, in which 19 Indian soldiers lost their lives. The anniversary highlights a decade of evolving national security measures. The government noted that the resolve shown in 2016 laid the groundwork for subsequent bold actions, including the 2019 Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor in 2025. In his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani yesterday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the 2016 surgical strike against terrorist hideouts as a historic milestone. He said the surgical strike highlighted the role of the Indian Army in carrying out the operation across the LoC. PM Modi recalled how the world was astonished by the manner in which Indian soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terrorism. The Prime Minister said that India’s counter-terrorism approach has continued to evolve over the past decade, citing the Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor as examples. PM Modi said the surgical strike was India’s decisive response to the long-standing pain the country had endured due to terrorist attacks. The Prime Minister said India had suffered from terrorist attacks for a long time, recalling a period when serial blasts had become a frequent occurrence in the country. Referring to terrorist attacks in September 2008, Mr Modi recalled the serial blasts in Delhi on September 13, 2008, in which several innocent people lost their lives. The Prime Minister also recalled the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks, which took place just weeks after the Delhi blasts. He said India’s approach to terrorism has changed and that the country now follows a “zero-tolerance policy against terrorism”.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 200 Nation pays tribute to Shaheed Bhagat Singh on his 119th birth anniversary
national_raw_news.content: The nation is celebrating the 119th birth anniversary of revolutionary Shaheed-e-Azam Bhagat Singh today. On this day in 1907, Bhagat Singh was born in Banga village in Lyallpur district of Punjab, now in Pakistan. Bhagat Singh was born into a family of revolutionaries and was the second among seven siblings. He was lovingly called ‘Bhaganwala’, meaning the lucky one. He proved his name by sacrificing himself for the freedom of the country along with Rajguru and Sukhdev. A state-level programme, entitled ‘Jashn-e-Inquilab’, has been scheduled at Punjab Agricultural University in Ludhiana to celebrate his birth anniversary through cultural events. People are also visiting his native village Khatkar Kalan in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar to pay their respects to the great son of the soil. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has paid tributes to freedom fighter Shaheed Bhagat Singh on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, PM Modi said that with indomitable courage and valour, Bhagat Singh infused new energy into the freedom movement. The Prime Minister said that Bhagat Singh’s spirit of sacrificing everything for the honour of the nation is a symbol of the courage and resolve of India’s youth. PM Modi also shared a video paying tribute to Bhagat Singh.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | Sports 57 Esha Singh wins silver in women’s 25m pistol at Asian Games
national_raw_news.content: In the Asian Games 2026 in Japan, India’s Esha Singh won the silver medal in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual competition at Aichi-Nagoya today. The 21-year-old shooter won the medal with 38 points to finish second. Indian athlete Pincky Balhara secured the bronze medal in the women’s under-78kg Kurash event at Aichi-Nagoya today. She won the medal after defeating South Korea’s Lim Garam 3-0 in the quarter-finals. Earlier, the Indian men’s cricket team entered the semi-finals without taking the field after its quarter-final against Afghanistan was abandoned due to inclement weather at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan today. The defending champion side made it to the last four as it is ranked number one in the ICC T20I rankings, while Afghanistan is currently placed 10th. India will take on the winner of the quarter-final between Nepal and Sri Lanka in the semi-final. In the women’s boxing event, Indian Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain secured a medal in the 75-kilogram category with a 5-0 quarter-final win over South Korea’s Seong Suyeon. India are currently placed 12th in the medal standings, with an overall tally of 39 medals, including four gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Esha Singh on winning the silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, President Murmu said that her exceptional performance reflected great skill, precision and consistency. The President added that this medal is a proud addition to her sporting journey.

national_raw_news.title: Centre to send teams to Karnataka, Maharashtra to assess drought situation 2 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The Centre will dispatch teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation in the two states. Talking to reporters in New Delhi after the inaugural session of the National Conference on Agriculture for Rabi Campaign 2026, Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the governments of Maharashtra and Karnataka have declared drought in large parts of their states. He said that a Central team will be sent to Karnataka on 3rd October to assess the drought situation. The Minister said that the Central Government stands firmly with the states in this situation. The Minister added that there were initial concerns that the El Niño effect could reduce the sowing area and pose significant challenges. However, Mr Chouhan said that the country has almost met its Kharif sowing targets. Mr Chouhan reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to ensuring adequate availability of fertilisers across the country. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for ensuring adequate fertiliser availability despite challenging circumstances. The Minister also emphasised the importance of balanced use of fertilisers to protect soil health. He announced that a nationwide campaign, Khet Bachao Abhiyan, will be undertaken to ensure that fertiliser application is based on Soil Health Card recommendations, specifically addressing nutrient deficiencies in the soil.
